where: Section 1 (derivation), Section 2 (Abel's identity), Exam traps, Quiz Q4
problem: The exponential factor is written in plain text as "e−∫P dx" in several body paragraphs, for example "w = C e−∫P dx/y₁²" and "W = W₀ e−∫P dx". Rendered on a phone this reads as e minus ∫P dx, not as e raised to the power −∫P dx, so the main formula of the chapter is ambiguous everywhere except in the one formula block that uses <sup>.
fix: Use the superscript tag in every occurrence: w = C e<sup>−∫P dx</sup>/y₁², W = W₀e<sup>−∫P dx</sup>, y₂ = y₁∫ e<sup>−∫P dx</sup>/y₁² dx.

problem: "W₀ is the value of the Wronskian at any convenient point" conflicts with Section 1, which says the inner ∫P dx is any antiderivative. If the antiderivative is shifted by a constant, the constant W₀ is rescaled, so W₀ equals W(x₀) only when the lower limit of the integral is that point x₀.
fix: Say: take ∫P dx to mean ∫ from x₀ to x of P dx; then W₀ = W(x₀), the Wronskian evaluated at the chosen point x₀.

problem: It calls e<sup>−∫P dx</sup> "the same integrating factor as above". It is the factor inside the reduction-of-order integral, not an integrating factor; the integrating factor of the first-order equation for w is y₁²e<sup>∫P dx</sup>, which is different.
fix: Say: "e<sup>−∫P dx</sup> is the same exponential factor that appears in the reduction formula above."

problem: The shape x²y″ + a x y′ + b y = f(x) never says that a and b are constants. Without that, the reader cannot see why the substitution gives a constant-coefficient equation.
fix: Write: a Cauchy-Euler equation is x²y″ + a x y′ + b y = f(x), where a and b are constants.
